posts.author: inaki
posts.content_md:
I’d just like to introduce myself, my name is Inaki and actually this is the first time I’ve ever been on a forum or chatline on the internet. So, it will take a bit of getting used to. I’m not even sure if this message will get posted! I’ve been in holography now for quite a number of years, and I specialize in multicolour reflection work. Have a look at my new website, [http://www.inaki.co.uk](http://www.inaki.co.uk) when you have a moment. 

Its good to finally be on board! Cheers,

Inaki.

posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md:
Inaki is rather modest. For my money he makes the best pseudocolor holograms in the business. His attention to detail in every stage is what makes the final hologram so beautiful. At the Wales exhibition almost everyone would name his holograms amongst their favorites. OK Inaki, next drink's on you. 

Inaki, you never told me you made multicolor holograms with different lasers. I am amazed to see these photos. I thought you only did pseudocolor (or controlled color).

posts.author: inaki
posts.content_md:
Many thanks everyone for your really positive comments. I use plates made by Colour Holographics, the earlier stuff in the gallery on my website (upto about the year 2000, eg lalique glass, Beano) was made on material by HRT Gmbh, who then sold onto Colour. 

Thanks Kaveh, Melles Griot sent me a small 532 DPSS laser to try out sometime back. I only had it for a few weeks and couldn’t resist trying out some (almost) true colour with red and the green. Results were good, but there were some very small fringes generated by the green component, not noticeable in the photo but there. It was so consistent I think it must have been something in the electronic circuitry. Again, I was using Colour Holographics plates for these (early Panchromatic plates). Great contrast.
